abidjan-riviera-2-shop-workers-unpaid-wa.whole: The project rebuilt city services in Abidjan and other towns after years of conflict. By the Bank's own count at closing in March 2014, 5,750,000 city residents were given access to improved water sources against a revised target of 4,500,000, 35,586 new piped household water connections were made, and 3,230,000 people were brought within 500 metres of an all-season road. The same report records 21,500 new sewer connections against a target of 350,000, and no reduction in the waste water discharged into the Abidjan lagoon. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
abidjan-riviera-2-shop-workers-unpaid-wa.searched: Cached completion report ICR00003208 (results framework, pp. viii-xi) and evaluation review ICRR14735; web search for an Ivorian audit or utility figure on the project.

kribi-gas-plant-land-and-crops-taken-mpo.whole: The Kribi plant started selling power in May 2013, adding 216 megawatts of nameplate capacity to a national system of about 933 megawatts. The World Bank's completion report records generation of 532 gigawatt hours in 2013, 1,197 in 2014, 1,261 in 2015 and 1,116 in 2016, against a long-term target of 1,127 a year. The same report records the CFA 40 billion local bank loan, about US$82 million, that the IDA guarantee was designed to make possible as raised in full. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
kribi-gas-plant-land-and-crops-taken-mpo.searched: Cached completion report for P110177 (paras 34, 46, Figure 3). ARSEL 2021 activity report opened directly: the specific-consumption table gives the KPDC figures but states no unit in any column header, so the figures were dropped.

pdue-cameroon-unpaid-compensation-yaound.whole: The urban upgrading project worked in Yaoundé, Douala, Bamenda, Maroua and Mbalmayo. By the Bank's own count at closing in August 2015, 63.2 kilometres of city roads and 108.5 kilometres of drainage had been built or rehabilitated, against revised targets of 41 and 49 kilometres, and 435,263 people had been brought within 500 metres of an all-season road. On the water side the same report records 35,411 subsidised household connections against a target of 70,000, 82 community water points against a target of 1,200 after the standpost activity was cancelled, and the water sector's financial balance not restored. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
pdue-cameroon-unpaid-compensation-yaound.searched: Cached completion report for P084002 (results framework, pp. iv-vii) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for a Cameroonian audit figure.

drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.whole: The works reopened roads in Équateur and Katanga. By the Bank's own count at closing in June 2012, 360 kilometres of road had been rehabilitated, against 522 kilometres planned at approval and 360 after the 2010 restructuring. The report says the drive from Lubumbashi to Kasenga fell from 60 hours to 3, that truck access to Gemena fell from about a week to one or two days, that 1,891,932 more rural people were within reach of an all-season road, and that the project paid for 3.5 million days of labour-intensive work. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
drc-rn5-rn6-rn2-compensation-arrears.searched: Cached completion report for P088619 (results framework, pp. vii-ix) and its evaluation review; web search for Congolese road agency or audit figures.

drc-urban-project-injury-threats-and-wor.whole: The project funded roads, drainage and erosion works in nine Congolese cities and a performance grant scheme for city governments. By the Bank's own count at closing in July 2021, 406,911 people had improved urban living conditions against a revised target of 391,000, and 31.81 kilometres of city road had been rehabilitated against a revised target of 31.8 kilometres, raised from 11.9 kilometres at appraisal. Of US$190 million originally committed, US$108.2 million was disbursed; the performance-based investment sub-component spent US$6.4 million of the US$70 million planned after the additional financing, and four cities met the performance conditions. The figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
drc-urban-project-injury-threats-and-wor.searched: Cached completion report for P129713 (data sheet, paras 14-16, Annex 1) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for a Congolese audit figure.

kinshasa-water-works-land-and-houses-tak.whole: The project paid for water works, road rehabilitation and school grants in Kinshasa and Bandundu. By the Bank's own count at closing in May 2013, 216,000 people in the target areas had access to improved water sources against a target of 239,000, 86 community standposts were built or rehabilitated against a target of 80, and 85.3 kilometres of water network were laid against a target of 140 kilometres. The same report records 40.2 kilometres of city road rehabilitated and 1,300,000 people brought within 500 metres of an all-season road, against a target of 800,000. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
kinshasa-water-works-land-and-houses-tak.searched: Cached completion report for P104497 (results framework, pp. vii-ix) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for REGIDESO or Congolese audit figures.

colombia-water-easements-unsettled-at-cl.whole: The loan paid for water and sewer sub-projects in municipalities across Colombia. The Bank's completion report counts 1,520,554 people living where the infrastructure was upgraded, against a target of 1.2 million, with 44,205 people newly connected to urban water networks against a target of 40,000 and 25,773 newly connected to urban sewer networks against a target of 60,000. It adds that no monitoring system was set up at sub-project level, so how far the works improved service is unclear. A later field review by the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group, still the lender's own office, found water coverage in the project areas up to 85 percent by 2014 against a national average of 95 percent, sewerage connections up 30 percent from the project's start, and sewerage coverage averaging 60 percent against a target of 87 percent, with no sewerage works carried out at all in ten sub-projects.
colombia-water-easements-unsettled-at-cl.searched: Cached completion report for P082973 (results framework, pp. iii-iv) and the Independent Evaluation Group's Project Performance Assessment Report of 29 December 2016; web search for Contraloría General or Superservicios figures.

riohacha-wayuu-lagoon-resettlement.whole: The loan paid for water and sewer works across La Guajira. By the Bank's own count at closing in 2018, 409,160 urban residents had access to improved water sources against a target of 357,285, water ran for an average of 11.4 hours a day against 8 hours before the project and a revised target of 14, and metering reached 51 percent of households against a target of 81 percent. The wastewater lagoons the works were meant to feed were not finished: the completion report puts the Riohacha lagoon contract at 9 percent complete at closing, and records wastewater treatment targets met in Barrancas and Fonseca and exceeded in San Juan del Cesar and Villanueva while the average share of wastewater treated across the project areas fell from 20 percent to 14 percent. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
riohacha-wayuu-lagoon-resettlement.searched: Cached completion report for P096965 (paras 24-35, Table 3, contract table for Contract 239-2015) and its evaluation review; Spanish-language searches for Contraloría or Colombian press reporting on the El Encanto lagoon returned only other Riohacha water contracts.

djibouti-ambouli-dike-resettlement.whole: The credit paid to repair damage from the April 2004 floods in Djibouti city. By the Bank's own count, 2.5 kilometres of the Ambouli flood protection dike were rebuilt with erosion control works and finished in March 2009, and the report says the dike should hold a flood of up to 1,500 cubic metres a second if it is maintained. The same report records 14 paved roads, 2 bridges, 5 kilometres of stormwater channels and 500 manholes rehabilitated. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
djibouti-ambouli-dike-resettlement.searched: Cached completion report for P089968 (results framework, pp. iii-v) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for Djiboutian government or donor flood-protection figures.

canal-neyba-arroyo-rico-expropriations.whole: The loan paid to repair irrigation, dams and power works after storms. By the Bank's own count at closing in October 2016, irrigation service had been restored on 37,218 hectares against a target of 12,000, 152 kilometres of transmission line had been rebuilt, and 252 megawatts of hydro capacity had been restored against a revised target of 254. Of four dams to be rehabilitated three were done, while works on the Maguaca dam were in litigation with 16 percent complete at closing, and 14 of 64 new hydrological and weather monitoring stations are recorded as partly vandalised, then stored and repaired for re-installation. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
canal-neyba-arroyo-rico-expropriations.searched: Cached completion report for P109932 (results framework, pp. ix-x) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for Cámara de Cuentas or INDRHI figures.

manta-properties-taken-without-agreement.whole: The loan paid for water, sewer and street works in Manta. By the Bank's own count, water ran for an average of 19.3 hours a day against 14 hours before the project and a target of 24, 23,024 people were given paved access to their houses in lower-income neighbourhoods, and 15,740 household sewer connections were covered by rehabilitation works. The utility's working ratio, the share of revenue taken up by running costs, fell from 88 percent to 85 percent against a revised target of 70 percent, and travel time along the Par Vial corridor fell from 15 to 13 minutes against a target of 10. The project closed in December 2020; these are the lender's own figures, taken from the project unit, and no independent check was found.
manta-properties-taken-without-agreement.searched: Cached completion report for P143996 (Annex 1 results indicators) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for Ecuador's Contraloría General or EPAM Manta figures.

lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.whole: By the Bank's own count, 1,760 kilometres of fibre optic cable had been laid by the project's close in October 2020, linking 26 towns to Libreville and reaching the borders of Congo, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea. The first 1,140 kilometres has been sold commercially since February 2019; the 620-kilometre extension was finished in March 2020 but was not yet being sold when the project closed. The same report puts the wholesale price of an international 2 megabit link to Europe down from US$10,500 to US$273 a month, and retail internet down from US$218 to US$6 per megabit a month. The United Nations Statistical Yearbook, using International Telecommunication Union figures, puts the share of people in Gabon using the internet at 13.0 percent in 2010, 45.8 percent in 2015 and 71.7 percent in 2021, while the completion report quotes ITU figures of 24 percent for 2012 and 62 percent for 2019.
lalara-fibre-assets-destroyed.searched: Cached completion report for P122776 (PDO 1-3 sections, Annex 1); UN Statistical Yearbook table 30 on internet usage, drawn from the ITU database, for an independent penetration figure.

dartlo-telavi-rehabilitation-compensatio.whole: The project paid for roads, water and heritage works in Kakheti to draw tourists. By the Bank's own count at closing in December 2017, 26.3 kilometres of road had been built or rehabilitated against a target of 20, and 907 households had piped water connections from the works against a target of 500. The same report counts points of sale in the renovated heritage sites and towns rising from 248 to 337 against a target of 323, and US$61 million of private investment against a target of US$50 million. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.

igoeti-sveneti-highway-worker-death-and-.whole: The credit paid to upgrade 48 kilometres of the east-west highway between Igoeti and Sveneti. By the Bank's own count at closing in June 2012 the full 48 kilometres were built, and the drive between the two points fell from 19 minutes to 11.8. The same report puts operating costs for a car at US$0.18 a kilometre against US$0.20 before the works, and for a truck at US$0.71 against US$0.76, and records road deaths per 10,000 cars falling from 14.5 to 6.8 by the end of 2011. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
igoeti-sveneti-highway-worker-death-and-.searched: Cached completion report for P094044 (results framework, pp. vii-x) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for Georgian Roads Department or State Audit Office figures.

kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.whole: The project paid to modernise Ghana's land registries, including a new office for the land sector agencies in Kumasi. By the Bank's own count, 82,438 land transactions had been registered by the end of 2019 against a target of 30,000, and the time to register a deed in the reformed offices fell from three months to 2.11 months against a target of one month. The same report says the time to register a land title could not be reported because the baseline and target were found to be unclear and inaccurately reported, and that spending on the component paying for the Kumasi building and project management reached US$17.16 million against US$10.78 million planned. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
kumasi-lands-office-farmers-displaced.searched: Cached completion report ICR00005225 for P120636 (paras 18, 1389, Annex 1) and the two evaluation reviews; web search for Ghana Audit Service or Lands Commission figures.

bijilo-cable-route-compensation-unpaid.whole: The grant paid The Gambia's membership fees for the Africa Coast to Europe submarine cable, a landing station that reached 10 gigabits a second, and internet links for 36 government bodies and six secondary schools. By the Bank's count, drawing on the government's own completion report, the share of Gambians with access to internet service rose from 0.75 percent in 2010 to 28 percent by the country's part of the project closing in 2016, against a target of 3 percent; the United Nations Statistical Yearbook, using International Telecommunication Union figures, puts internet use in The Gambia at 9.2 percent in 2010, 17.6 percent in 2015 and 33.0 percent in 2021. The same report puts the wholesale price of an international 2 megabit link to Europe down from US$5,000 to US$500 a month, and the business price of a megabit a month down 73 percent, from US$1,500 to about US$400. Its own calculation puts the internal rate of return on the cable investment at 38 percent, with a net present value of US$17 million.

honduras-road-rehabilitation-ii-land-tak.whole: The credit paid to rebuild primary and secondary roads. By the Bank's own count at closing in May 2015, 127 kilometres had been returned to good condition; the target was up to 200 kilometres at approval in 2008, was raised to 300 kilometres with the 2009 additional financing, and was cut to 143 kilometres at the 2013 restructuring to cover only the works the credits would pay for. The same report puts vehicle operating costs down 36 to 42 percent on the San Lorenzo to Olanchito road and 37 to 44 percent on El Porvenir to Marale. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
honduras-road-rehabilitation-ii-land-tak.searched: Cached completion report for P109058 (results framework, pp. iii-v); no evaluation review harvested; web search for Honduras's Tribunal Superior de Cuentas or INSEP figures.

cap-labadie-road-compensation-escrow.whole: The grant paid for earthquake recovery works, among them the road from Cap-Haitien to Labadie. By the Bank's own count at closing in June 2018, 8.5 kilometres of that road were built for US$8.2 million of works, and the road accounted for 45,000 of the 95,000 days of local paid labour the project generated. Across the project, 100 kilometres of road were stabilised or rehabilitated, matching the revised target, and 1.1 million people were counted as benefiting from repaired infrastructure. The completion report's own after-the-fact calculation puts the road's economic rate of return at 27 percent, against the 14 percent estimated when the financing was approved, and notes the two rest on different methods; both figures are the lender's, and no independent check was found.
cap-labadie-road-compensation-escrow.searched: Cached completion report for P120895 (paras 44, 52, cost annex, Annex 1) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for Haiti's Cour Supérieure des Comptes figures.

lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.whole: The loan paid to widen and strengthen national roads in western Sumatra. By the Bank's own count at closing in June 2021, 578 kilometres of national road had been improved, which matched the revised target after cancelled road packages but was below the 715 kilometres targeted at the start. The same report puts daily traffic on the project roads at 14,490 vehicles against 7,505 before the works and a target of 14,544, operating costs down 8 percent for a car, 18 percent for a bus and 14 percent for a heavy truck, and travel time for light vehicles down 21 percent. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.searched: Cached completion report for P090990 (Annex 1 results indicators, paras 886-889) and evaluation review ICRR; web search for BPK audit or Bina Marga figures.
